C0=C_B(2/B)^(1/p-1/r) is exactly the constant in (15), so sigma<=sqrt(delta)C0 epsilon_J is correct. The parameter set is nonempty: 1/2<theta<min(1-a/2,(3-a-alpha)/2) and 1/(1-theta)<r<2/a force 2<r, and p in [1/theta,2) gives 1<nu=1/theta<=p<2<r. The CM space is {L Phi: Phi in H_seen} with norm ||Phi||_H, matching the first-chaos definition printed on page 190 (H={E(X.Z)}, ||h||=E(Z^2)^(1/2)). Because L kills H_seen^perp, the raw-H operator norm bound is the true embedding norm bound. Accepted Sections 5 and 7 and target lines 39-40, 80, 85 exclude raw L2 and trace-class fields.

checks.claim: C2: E Y<=C g_delta uniformly in J follows from marginal variance contraction, all p moments, the F extension, stopping and delta n<=2/B, without block independence.
checks.reason: Y_(m,J)(f)=W((I-P_J)T_(delta,m)f) has variance <=||f||^2 because T is an isometry and I-P_J is a contraction on H_W. Source-operator-convergence Theorem 1 (3) with C=1 and actual-operator-driver (4) on [0,B] give a marginal Lp(Ctheta) bound independent of delta, m and J. The bounded map M->M L_psi (fixed-mask Section 3) carries this to F, and stopping with constant extension does not raise the Holder norm. Then E Y<=(E Y^p)^(1/p)=(delta sum_m E||X_(m,J)||^p)^(1/p)<=(delta n)^(1/p)C g_delta. Also n=N+1<=2/(delta B) because delta B<1. Only linearity of expectation over the blocks is used. g_delta->0 because a<1.

checks.claim: C3: the tuple has a separable Banach Radon centered Gaussian law, with closed support, CM density and genuine AWS assumptions, reached through finite projections and transfer rather than inverse covariance, RNP or trace-class shortcuts.
checks.reason: The planned route is sound, and these remain proof obligations, as the target says. Finite coefficient sums in the same W converge in Lp, so every continuous linear functional is an L2 limit of centered Gaussians, and separability gives a Radon law. Support can be proved inside the packet. Put E0=closure of L(H_seen). If l vanishes on E0 then l(L k_l)=||k_l||^2=0, so l(X)=0 a.s., and a countable separating family gives X in E0 a.s. CM density in E0 holds by definition. The E0={0} case is the zero case. No covariance inverse is needed. The printed pages do not define abstract Wiener space, so restricting to E0 is the correct safeguard.

checks.claim: C4: primary Theorem 11.7 and Example 11.8 apply with f=g=norm, b=2EY, mu(A_b)>=1/2, sigma=C0 sqrt(delta)epsilon_J, the all-x/all-h shift inequality, measurable enlargement and correct zero cases.
checks.reason: Hypotheses read from both images and matched to the excerpt: a,sigma in (0,infinity); measurable f,g; mu(A_a)>0; (11.8) off a null set for all h; tail Phibar(a-bar+r/sigma) for r>a, with a-bar=a-hat-a/sigma. Page 190 prints Phibar(y)<=exp(-y^2/2) for y>=0. With a=b=2EY>0, Markov gives mu(Y<=b)>=1/2, so a-hat>=0 (a-hat=+infinity is allowed). For r=b+sigma t, t>0, a-bar+r/sigma=a-hat+t>=t, giving P(Y>b+sigma t)<=exp(-t^2/2) with no prefactor. The triangle inequality gives (11.8) with N empty for every x and h, and any sigma>=embedding norm works. Measurability: L=(bounded primitive map)composed with T(I-P_J) is compact because T is compact, so K=L(unit ball of H) is compact, A_b is closed, and A_b+rK is closed and hence Borel; the outer-measure convention of footnote 3 is unnecessary. Zero cases: EY=0 means Y=0 a.s. and the theorem is not invoked. epsilon_J=0 implies L=0, hence k_l=0 for all l and X=0 a.s. So EY>0 forces epsilon_J>0 and sigma>0, and the positive-sigma source is not misused. The independent-component rough-path theorem is not imported.

checks.claim: C5: tail integration, Rayleigh domination and the scalar Young bound retain the Gaussian quadratic with correct prefactor, A_nu, eta and epsilon powers and real AMGM guards.
checks.reason: Independently derived. P(Y>y)<=P(b+sigma R>y) for all y, so for nondecreasing phi E phi(Y)<=E phi(b+sigma R) by layer cake, with no noise replacement or conditional independence. Convexity gives (b+sigma R)^nu<=2^(nu-1)(b^nu+sigma^nu R^nu). Put A=eta 2^(nu-1)(C0 epsilon_J)^nu and x=sqrt(delta)R; then (eta/delta)2^(nu-1)sigma^nu R^nu=A x^nu/delta. Weighted AMGM with weights nu/2,(2-nu)/2 and bases x^2/(2nu),A^(2/(2-nu))(2nu)^(nu/(2-nu)) has geometric mean exactly A x^nu and arithmetic mean x^2/4+S, where S=(2-nu)/2 (2nu)^(nu/(2-nu))A^(2/(2-nu))=A_nu eta^(2/(2-nu))(C0 epsilon_J)^(2nu/(2-nu)), with exactly the stated A_nu. The retained quadratic gives E exp(R^2/4)=integral of t exp(-t^2/4)dt=2, exactly the delta log2 term. The Lean type in mathlib-young-type-v1.txt matches: w1,w2,p1,p2>=0, w1+w2=1, p1^w1 p2^w2<=w1p1+w2p2. Weights are strictly positive for 1<nu<2, so the Real.rpow 0^0 case never occurs. A=0 or x=0 gives LHS 0 because exponents are positive, and rpow products need nonnegative bases, which hold. The natural-power FiniteYoung lemma is correctly disclaimed. The target's stanza leaves A and t undefined (see minor findings).
